record.paper_title: On some open questions in bilinear quantum control
record.context_brief: Good Galerkin approximations beyond weak coupling
record.original_question: Does there exist a bilinear quantum system dψ/dt = (A + u(t)B)ψ in which the control operator B is unbounded, the pair (A,B) satisfies Assumption 1, the system is not k-weakly-coupled for any k > 0, and nevertheless the infinite-dimensional dynamics can still be approximated uniformly by its Galerkin truncations with respect to the L^1 norm of the control? Here the intended uniform approximation is the same type discussed earlier in the paper for weakly-coupled systems, where for every control with bounded L^1 norm the Galerkin evolution stays uniformly close to the full evolution.

evidence.quote: Remark 1: Notice that, in Propositions 7 and 8, the upper bound of the |A|k/2 norm of the solution of (1) or the bound on the error between the infinite dimensional system and its finite dimensional approximation only depend on the L1 norm of the control, not on the time.

Question 5: Does it exist a system (A, B) with unbounded B that satisfies Assumption 1, is not k-weakly-coupled for any k > 0 and that can be approached, uniformly with respect of the L1 norm of the control, by its Galerkin approximations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a bilinear control system on an infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space H of the form

    dψ/dt = (A + u(t) B) ψ,    ψ(t) ∈ H,    u : [0,T] → R,

where A is a (densely defined) skew-adjoint operator with purely discrete spectrum and an orthonormal basis (φ_n)_{n≥1} of eigenvectors A φ_n = i λ_n φ_n, and B is a (possibly unbounded) skew-symmetric operator. Assume the standing hypothesis (Assumption 1):

  (i) A is skew-adjoint with discrete spectrum {i λ_n};
  (ii) there exists an orthonormal basis (φ_n) of eigenvectors of A contained in the domain of B;
  (iii) for every u ∈ R, A + u B generates a strongly continuous unitary group on H.

For k > 0 define the operator |A|^{k/2} via functional calculus on the spectrum of A. The system (A,B) is called k-weakly-coupled if the domain of |A|^{k/2} is invariant under the propagators of A + uB and there exists C_k > 0 such that

    | Re ⟨ |A|^k ψ, B ψ ⟩ | ≤ C_k ⟨ |A|^{k/2} ψ, |A|^{k/2} ψ ⟩

for all ψ in the domain of |A|^{k/2}.

For N ≥ 1 let Π_N be the orthogonal projection onto span(φ_1,…,φ_N), and let ψ^N(t) denote the solution of the Galerkin truncation

    dψ^N/dt = Π_N (A + u(t) B) Π_N ψ^N,    ψ^N(0) = Π_N ψ(0).

Say that (A,B) admits good Galerkin approximations uniformly in the L^1 norm of the control if, for every ε > 0, every R > 0, and every initial datum φ_n, there exists N_0 such that for all N ≥ N_0 and all locally integrable controls u with ‖u‖_{L^1} ≤ R one has

    sup_{t ≥ 0} ‖ ψ(t) − ψ^N(t) ‖_H < ε,

with the bound depending only on ‖u‖_{L^1} and not on t.

Question. Does there exist a pair (A,B) with B unbounded that satisfies Assumption 1, is not k-weakly-coupled for any k > 0, yet still admits good Galerkin approximations uniformly in the L^1 norm of the control in the sense above?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search returned the foundational works of Boussaid–Caponigro–Chambrion on weakly-coupled systems and good Galerkin approximations, plus follow-up works (e.g., obstructions to bilinear control of Gross–Pitaevskii with unbounded potentials), but no source explicitly resolves the question of whether a non-k-weakly-coupled system with unbounded B satisfying Assumption 1 can still be uniformly L^1-approximated by Galerkin truncations. Status appears to remain open/unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Weakly-coupled systems in quantum control (HAL)
status_evidence.snippet: Weakly coupled systems ... can be precisely approached by finite dimensional Galerkin approximations.
status_evidence.claim: Defines the framework of weakly-coupled systems and good Galerkin approximations relevant to the question.

status_evidence.title: Obstruction to the bilinear control of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation: an example with an unbounded potential
status_evidence.snippet: Example with unbounded potential illustrating obstructions in bilinear quantum control.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work studies unbounded B but does not settle the L^1-uniform Galerkin approximation question for non-weakly-coupled systems.
